**Parent:** LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI (When a request cannot be processed because there are no available models include a retry timer)
**Type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Problem

The proxy emits a truthful multi-hour `Retry-After` on the "All providers
exhausted" 503. Whether that timer is actually honoured depends on the
ContextHub client, which previously clamped every applied `Retry-After` to
60 s. The linked client item WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM was created for that gap
(producer decision Q3a). The proxy item must record the cross-link and verify
that the client-side honouring landed, so the composed contract is
demonstrably intact from the client's perspective.

## Change

Record and verify the cross-repository link: confirm the ContextHub change
honours long server hints and record the evidence (file/line/default plus its
tests) on this work item. Do not edit the ContextHub repository from this
item; if a residual client gap remains, raise a new linked work item instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC6 — Client gap linked:** The ContextHub item WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM exists and
  is referenced from this item, so the proxy's honest multi-hour timer can be
  honoured by the client rather than clamped to 60 s.
- The cross-link comment on this work item records the client-side evidence: `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts` exposes `serverHintMaxDelayMs` (default 6 h) and no longer clamps a server hint to `maxDelayMs`, with covering tests named.
- Any residual client-side gap is raised as a new work item and recorded as a blocking/related link (not silently folded into this item).

## Minimal implementation

- Inspect the ContextHub recovery module and record the exact file, symbol, default value and covering test names as evidence.
- Add a comment on `LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI` with the cross-references and evidence, and the outcome of the verification (gap closed / residual gap).
- Confirm the ContextHub item in `WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM` already references this proxy item; add a reciprocal note only if the item is still open.

## Dependencies

- None (cross-repository evidence gathering); may proceed in parallel with the test item.

## Key Files

- ContextHub `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts` — `serverHintMaxDelayMs`, `calculateDelay` (read-only, not edited here).
- ContextHub `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-after.test.ts` — long-hint coverage (read-only).
- `proxy/README.md` — referencing doc target for the client expectation (owned by the docs sibling item).

## Deliverables

- A verification comment on this work item with the cross-links and quoted client evidence.

data.description:
## Blocker

`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` aborts during `resolve_api_keys` because `MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY` is neither set in the environment nor resolvable from `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`. The proxy, llama-server (8080) and TTS server (8081) are therefore all down, and every mode fails identically because the key is declared for models `plan`, `author` and `code` in the base `config.yaml` (inherited by the `config-fast.yaml` and `config-cheap.yaml` overlays via `config_merge.load_merged`).

Discovered while investigating why the LP-0MVAZPQUM006EAC7 slot sweep returned 0/12 completed / 12 errors (see `logs/proxy-benchmark.log` and `slot_benchmark_summary.txt`: 'llama-server failed to become ready at 1 slots').

## Evidence

- `curl http://localhost:8000/health` -> connection refused; nothing listening on 8000/8080/8081.
- No `uvicorn proxy.server` / `llama-server` processes running.
- `bash scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart` exits at the key check with:
  `MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY  (required by: plan, author, code)`.
- `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` has `munitoai` (which resolves `MUNITOAI_API_KEY`) but no `munitoai-free` / `munitoai_free` entry, and the resolver maps `MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY` -> auth key `munitoai_free` (or `munitoai-free`).

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the fast/cheap proxy profiles to start unattended on this
host again, so that local-agent traffic and GPU benchmarks (including the slot
sweep) can run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY` is resolvable by `start-proxy.sh` — either added to `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` under `munitoai-free` (type `api_key`) or supplied via the environment — without committing the secret to the repository.
- `bash proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart` completes and `curl -s http://localhost:8000/health` reports `status: healthy` with `llama_server_running: true`, `tts_server_running: true` and `tts_server_healthy: true`.
- The reason `start-proxy.sh` aborts on an unresolved key is recorded (intended fail-loud behaviour) and, if the resolver is judged to mis-map `munitoai-free`, the fix is covered by a test.

## Notes

- Requires operator input: the key value itself cannot be invented or recovered by an agent.
- Operator decision needed on whether `munitoai-free` should remain a required provider for `plan`/`author`/`code`, or be dropped from the required-key set.
data.title: Proxy cannot start: MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY unresolved (blocks slot sweep)

data.description:
## Problem

`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` resolves `api_key_env` names to `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`
keys by lowercasing the env var name and stripping the `_api_key` suffix, then doing an
**exact dictionary lookup** with no hyphen/underscore normalisation:

```python
key = key_name.lower()            # MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY -> 'munitoai_free_api_key'
if key.endswith('_api_key'):
    stem = key[:-8]               # -> 'munitoai_free'
    if stem in auth and ...       # exact match only
```

Because of this, the documented key name `munitoai-free` (hyphen) can never resolve
`MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY` — only `munitoai_free` (underscore) does.

`proxy/config.yaml:254` documents the opposite:

> `(``munitoai-free`` → ``MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY``)`

So an operator following the config comment adds `munitoai-free` to `auth.json`, the
proxy still refuses to start, and the failure appears identical to a genuinely missing
key. This was the actual root cause of the outage that blocked LP-0MVAZPQUM006EAC7;
it was only found by reading the resolver source after the "obvious" fix failed.

## Goal

As an operator, I want the documented auth.json key name for a provider to be the one
the resolver actually accepts, so that adding a key per the docs works first time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test pins the env-var -> auth.json key mapping, covering both the hyphenated
  documented form (`munitoai-free`) and the underscore form (`munitoai_free`) for
  `MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY`, and asserting the resulting behaviour is intentional.
- A single documented convention is agreed and enforced in one place:
  either `resolve_from_auth_json` normalises hyphens/underscores (so both names work),
  or the config comment and docs are corrected to state the underscore form.
- `proxy/config.yaml:254` no longer contradicts the resolver's actual lookup rule.
- The failure message for an unresolved key names the exact auth.json key(s) that
  would have satisfied it, so the mismatch is self-diagnosing.

## Notes

- Discovered-from: LP-0MVBJPQE50017BGL (proxy outage: MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY unresolved).
- Immediate operator workaround already applied: `munitoai_free` added to
  `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` with the same key as `munitoai`; proxy verified healthy
  and the key verified accepted by `https://api.munito.ai/inference/v1/chat/completions` (HTTP 200).
- Related pattern: `OPENCODE_API_KEY` already has an explicit preference list
  (`opencode-go` over `opencode`) at the same call site — precedent for special-casing,
  which is exactly why the general rule should be documented or made symmetrical.
data.title: start-proxy.sh auth.json key lookup does not match the documented munitoai-free name

data.comment:
RESOLVED - root cause was NOT a missing key. Session ID: herdr-1792189917-2820042-19001 - /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-llm--/2026-10-16T22-31-57-493Z_herdr-1792189917-2820042-19001.jsonl

## Root cause

My first fix attempt (adding `munitoai-free` to auth.json, per the documented name) did not work. `resolve_from_auth_json` in `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` lowercases the env var name and strips the `_api_key` suffix, then does an **exact** dict lookup with no hyphen/underscore normalisation:

- `MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY` -> `munitoai_free_api_key` -> stem `munitoai_free` (underscore)
- `munitoai-free` (hyphen, the name documented at `proxy/config.yaml:254`) therefore never matches.

So the key had to be added under `munitoai_free`, not `munitoai-free`.

## Fix applied (operator-authorised)

- `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`: added `munitoai_free` = `{type: api_key, key: <copy of munitoai.key>}` (mode 600 preserved; backup at `auth.json.bak.20261016T233626`). The `munitoai-free` alias was also left in place.
- No secret committed to the repository.

## Verification

- Resolver test: `MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY` now resolves via suffix-strip (`munitoai_free`).
- `bash proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart` completes: `[env] MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY resolved from ~/.pi/agent/auth.json`, then `=== Starting proxy server ===`.
- `curl http://localhost:8000/health` -> `status: healthy`, `ready: true`, `llama_server_running: true`, `tts_server_running: true`, `tts_server_healthy: true`, `backend_reachable: true`.
- Copied key accepted by the free-tier endpoint: `POST https://api.munito.ai/inference/v1/chat/completions` (model `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash`, max_tokens=1) returned HTTP 200 with a real completion.

## AC status

- AC1 (key resolvable without committing the secret): MET.
- AC2 (start-proxy completes + healthy with llama + TTS): MET.
- AC3 (record reason; cover a resolver mis-map with a test): the resolver IS judged to mis-map the documented name, so the test is delegated to the follow-up defect item LP-0MVBJXZY5002UW10. Item left open pending that.
